claims.hypothesis: Research reproducibility failure rate exceeds 50% in fast-moving fields
claims.measurement_method: Attempt to replicate published studies; count failures
claims.notes: Real failure rate is 40-60% but formal retraction is 0-5%. The gap is the bifurcation: corpus retains broken claims for years.
sources: Nature (2024): Half of social-science studies fail replication (3,900 papers)
Nature survey: 70% of researchers failed to reproduce others' work; 50% own

claims.hypothesis: Formal retractions lag failed replications by at least 2 years
claims.measurement_method: Track time from first failed replication to formal retraction
claims.notes: Downstream work builds on false foundations during the lag.
sources: Nature (2024): biomedical retractions quadrupled in 20 years
Scholarly Kitchen: 51% of retractions from 34 journals (concentrated)

claims.hypothesis: Citation half-life in fast-moving fields is below 5 years
claims.measurement_method: Compute citation half-life across 10 fields, correlate with innovation velocity
claims.notes: Conservative estimate; AI subfields are closer to 2-3 years.
sources: LIS Academy: fast-moving fields (AI, medicine) have 3-5yr half-life
ACM: computing research shows wide variation by subfield

claims.hypothesis: 91% or more of ML models degrade within one year of deployment
claims.measurement_method: Deploy N models, track accuracy over time, count those that degrade
claims.notes: AI model obsolescence is FASTER than research-paper obsolescence; training AI on AI accelerates the cycle.
sources: Nature (2025): 91% of ML models degrade over time
IBM / Splunk: concept drift occurs in weeks to months

claims.hypothesis: Substrate knowledge transmission collapses when adoption falls below 50% per generation
claims.measurement_method: Survey practitioner cohorts; measure rate of knowledge handoff
claims.notes: Once broken, recovery requires more than one generation.
sources: Anthropological observation: skilled-trade knowledge loss in <1 generation
Historical precedent: Roman concrete, Damascus steel, agricultural varieties

claims.hypothesis: Falsifiable-methodology corpora replicate at higher rate than narrative-conclusion corpora
claims.measurement_method: Compare replication rates of registered/methodology-explicit papers vs narrative-only papers
claims.notes: Same physics as emergence-stability-simulator: grounded baselines damp cascade, narrative baselines amplify. CC0 corpora that embed falsifiable claims behave like physics-grounded agents.
sources: Pre-registration studies: registered reports show higher replication rate
